1Purpose

This policy sets out what [Provider name] does when a provider uses a in an emergency, or without . It covers a participant whose behaviour support plan we write or , or are engaged to write. We support the provider that used the practice, and we include the participant in the review of what happened. It is for participants, their families and advocates, the providers that implement our plans, our and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every practitioner, , manager and contractor who works for [Provider name] under our registration for specialist behaviour support.
  • Every participant we hold a plan for, or are engaged to write one for. For any other participant, we give the caller the safety and reporting advice in PRO-SBS-05 steps 4 and 9 without recording identifying details, and we offer the referral route in PRO-SBS-06 Interim Behaviour Support Plans Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support). We open no review for a participant we are not engaged for.
  • Every : a registered provider, an unregistered provider, or a person who supports the participant day to day.
  • It does not set the duties of the provider that used the practice. That provider makes the incident report, the notification to the NDIS Commission and the record of the use. A provider that also implements plans follows POL-BSP-07 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Policy (Implementing Behaviour Support Plans) for its own uses.

"The Incident Rules" in this policy means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.

"The Restrictive Practices Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.

3Commitments

C1

We will record every notice of an emergency or on the we hear of it, and open a review for it, whoever tells us, for every participant we hold a plan for or are engaged to write one for.

Where anyone was hurt or needed a medical check, we advise the 24-hour route, as the Commission's guidance expects. The advice also covers the record of the use, the , and authorisation and plan steps. We confirm the advice in writing within 1 business day.

4Ground rules

G1

We support the provider that used the practice. We do not take over its duties. The provider makes the incident report, the notification and the record of the use.

G2

Only the authorisation process of a state or territory authorises a practice. Our advice is never an authorisation. We never tell a provider to use a practice that the plan and the authorisation process do not allow.

G3

Only an NDIS behaviour support practitioner develops or changes a plan that contains a regulated restrictive practice (the Restrictive Practices Rules, sections 18 and 22). A manager, a worker, a family member or an implementing provider cannot.

G4

A participant who is hurt, or still being restrained, comes before any record. We say "call 000" first.

G5

When we cannot tell whether a use is reportable, we advise the provider to notify. The NDIS Commission can reclassify it.

G6

A review looks for causes, not for someone to blame. Nobody is punished for telling us about a use in good faith.

G7

The participant decides whether, and how, they take part. We respect "no". The review goes ahead without them, and we offer again later.

G8

Nobody at [Provider name] can extend a time limit that the law sets. The Service Manager can extend one of our own limits only for a reason written in the review record. We tell the participant.

G9

We keep each review record and its register entry for 7 years from the day it is closed (our standard). The Incident Rules, section 12(4), and the Restrictive Practices Rules, section 15(3), set 7 years from the day a record is made. Other law can require longer, for example for a record about a child. Corrections are a new version with a reason. Nothing is overwritten.

G10

In a sole practitioner business, the Practitioner holds the Service Manager, Quality Manager and Chief Executive roles and does what those roles do, with two exceptions. The external Clinical Supervisor, engaged in writing and named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register, does the Service Manager's checks on the Practitioner's own work, signs off every review, and makes any reportable-incident decision, and any decision to tell the NDIS Commission about a provider, with the Practitioner. REG-GOV-01 also names a cover practitioner, who takes notices while the Practitioner is away, and an independent contact for concerns, who hears any concern about the Practitioner.

G11

Where a time limit in the law of [state or territory] is shorter than one in this policy, the law applies.

G12

We ask each implementing provider to tell us of any emergency or unauthorised use within 1 business day. A use that we find in data, and were not told about, starts a review the day we find it.

G13

Where a use resulted in any harm to the participant, or anyone was hurt or needed a medical check, we advise the 24-hour route, as the Commission's guidance expects. We never judge by phone whether an injury is serious. If in doubt, we advise 24 hours.

9Words we use

540 words
regulated restrictive practice
one of five practices the Restrictive Practices Rules, section 6, name. They are seclusion, chemical restraint, mechanical restraint, physical restraint and environmental restraint. A locked cupboard, a medicine given mainly to change behaviour and a bed rail used to stop someone getting up are everyday examples.
emergency use
a use of a regulated restrictive practice in an unplanned emergency, to stop serious harm, when no plan and no authorisation covered it. The Restrictive Practices Rules say "single emergency use" in section 9(2)(a) and do not define it.
unauthorised use
a use that the authorisation of a state or territory did not cover, or that went outside the participant's behaviour support plan.
implementing provider
the provider, or the person, who supports the participant day to day and uses, or may use, a practice under the plan.
practitioner
an NDIS behaviour support practitioner, a person the Commissioner considers suitable to assess and to write plans (the Restrictive Practices Rules, section 5).
Clinical Lead
the senior Practitioner who owns clinical practice at [Provider name]. In a sole practitioner business, the Practitioner.
Clinical Supervisor
the experienced Practitioner who supervises a Practitioner's work and signs off each review. In a sole practitioner business, always someone outside [Provider name], engaged in writing.
Quality Manager
the person who decides whether to tell the NDIS Commission about a provider or a reportable incident, and sends the notice. In a sole practitioner business, the Practitioner, who makes that decision with the Clinical Supervisor.
interim plan past its end date
an interim plan whose end date has passed without a comprehensive plan or a new version replacing it. A comprehensive plan does not lapse: a late review is a breach of our registration conditions, not a lapse, and the plan stays in force until the new version is finalised.
reportable incident
one of six types the NDIS Act 2013, section 73Z(4), names. One type is the use of a restrictive practice other than in accordance with an authorisation of a state or territory.
authorisation
the approval that the law of a state or territory requires before a practice may be used. It is not our advice and it is not a plan.
review
our check of one emergency or unauthorised use. It is not a plan review.
plan review
the formal review of a plan by a practitioner. PRO-SBS-04 sets it.
concern route
the steps in PRO-SBS-04 that ask a provider in writing to put a problem right, and decide whether to tell the Commissioner.
support network
the family, friends, carers, advocates and others the participant chooses.
person with legal authority
a guardian, a nominee or another person the law allows to decide for the participant.
independent advocate
a person outside [Provider name] who speaks up for the participant's wishes and rights.
debrief
the meeting where the implementing provider's workers and managers work out what to learn and change. The provider writes down what came out of it.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. When we advise a provider on a time limit in the Incident Rules, we tell it to count every weekday, so the notice is never late.

1Purpose

The result: a provider that used a restrictive practice in an emergency, or without , gets our support straight away. The participant takes part in the of what happened. Every step can be shown from the review record.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SBS-06 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Policy (Specialist Behaviour Support), C1 to C14.

"The Incident Rules" here means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.

"The Restrictive Practices Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.

2When and who

Start when anyone tells us, or we find, that a was used in an emergency or without authorisation on a participant whose plan we hold or are engaged to write. For any other participant, give the caller the safety and reporting advice in steps 4 and 9 without recording identifying details, offer the referral route in PRO-SBS-06 Interim Behaviour Support Plans Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support), and open no review record.

An must tell a specialist provider when a change in circumstances means the plan needs review (the Restrictive Practices Rules, section 10(2)(b)). We may also hear from the participant, a family member, an advocate, another provider, the NDIS Commission, or the data in a .

Who acts:

  • Any worker who is told passes the notice on (step 1).
  • The Service Manager receives the notice, names the lead and the cover, and keeps the incident review entry in REG-SBS-01.
  • The practitioner supports the provider, includes the participant and leads the review. This is the NDIS behaviour support practitioner who holds the participant's plan.
  • The reads the findings and signs them off.
  • The opens the review record, watches the time limits, decides whether to tell the NDIS Commission about a provider under PRO-SBS-04, and closes the record.
  • The Chief Executive decides a concern when the Quality Manager is involved in it.

In a sole practitioner business, the practitioner holds the Service Manager, Quality Manager and Chief Executive roles and does what those roles do, with two exceptions. The external Clinical Supervisor named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register does the Service Manager's checks on the practitioner's own work, signs off every review, and makes any reportable-incident decision, and any decision to tell the NDIS Commission about a provider, with the practitioner. The cover practitioner named there takes notices when the practitioner is away. The independent contact for concerns hears any concern about the practitioner.

If our own worker used the practice, we are the provider that used it. Start with PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure, FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form and PRO-INC-02 Reportable Incidents Notification Procedure. A provider registered for plan implementation also follows PRO-BSP-08 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Procedure (Implementing Behaviour Support Plans). Then run this procedure for the practitioner's review.

3Before you start

  • You hold the participant's current plan, or you know that we hold none.
  • You can reach a manager at the implementing provider by phone and email.
  • You hold the participant's communication preferences (FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form) and consent record (FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form).
  • You know which authorisation process of [state or territory] applies where the participant lives.
  • You can open REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register.
  • You have the NDIS Commission's phone number: 1800 035 544.

4Watch out

  • Our advice is not an authorisation. Only the process of [state or territory] authorises a practice. A provider that hears "carry on" from us may keep using a practice that nobody has authorised.
  • The provider's clock started before ours. The provider's time to notify runs from when it became aware (the Incident Rules, sections 20(1)(a) and 21(1)(a)). We may hear on day 3 or on day 6. Check the date and advise at once.
  • A participant who is hurt needs help first. Do not wait for facts, forms or a manager. Waiting can make an injury worse.
  • A review can hurt the participant a second time. Asking someone to go over a restraint before they are ready causes distress and loses their trust. The participant chooses the time and the way.
  • What the participant says belongs to them. Sharing it with the provider, family or others without consent breaks their trust and can break privacy law.
  • A single can still mean the plan must change. Do not close a review because the use looks like a one-off.
  • We are not the participant's treating health practitioners. Never say that no medical check is needed. Never advise on a medicine dose. Do not coach a physical hold over the phone: physical techniques are taught only by a qualified trainer under PRO-SBS-03 Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Procedure.

  • the outcome was decided, signed off and told to the participant first
  • each action is done, or has moved into the plan review
  • the follow-up check found no further use, or a new review was opened.

These records now exist:

  • FRM-SBS-06, completed and signed, on the participant's behaviour support file for 7 years from the day it is closed
  • the incident review entry in REG-SBS-01
  • the written advice to the provider
  • an entry in REG-QMS-01, where an improvement was found
  • the plan review record or the interim plan record, where plan work started.

The provider's incident report, its notification and its record of the use stay with the provider.

  • Reach a manager at the provider within 1 business day (step 5)
  • Decide which duties apply, and treat doubt as reportable (step 7)

  • Raise a concern under PRO-SBS-04 if the provider cannot or will not act (step 14)
  • Ask the participant how they want to take part before you invite anyone else (step 16)

form.intro:
Use this record when [Provider name] is told that a was used in an emergency or without authorisation on a participant whose plan we write or review, or are engaged to write. For a participant we are not engaged for, we give the caller the safety and reporting advice in PRO-SBS-05 steps 4 and 9 without recording identifying details, offer the referral route in PRO-SBS-06, and do not open this record. One record follows one use, or one run of linked uses, from the notice to the follow-up check.

The record shows two things. The first is the support we gave the provider that used the practice. The second is how the participant, and the people they agreed to, took part in the review.

Who completes it:

  • Section A: the Quality Manager and the practitioner, from the first call.
  • Sections B to E: the practitioner who leads the review. The Quality Manager completes Q36, Q37 and Q38.
  • The Clinical Supervisor signs off the findings and the outcome.

Have ready: the participant's plan and the 's record of the use. Also have the participant's communication preferences (FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form) and their consent record (FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form).

This record is not the provider's incident report. It is not the notification to the NDIS Commission. The provider that used the practice makes both. If our own worker used the practice, complete FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form first.

If the answer at Q7 is "not reportable", the use is not an emergency or . Complete Section A, Q10, Q11 and Q14, which record the contact and the safety advice given, and leave Q12, Q13 and Q15 to Q36 empty. The Clinical Supervisor signs, and the Quality Manager closes the record at Q37 and Q38.

What happens next: the Service Manager copies the answers marked for REG-SBS-01 to the plan's incident review entry, one dated entry per review on the incident review sheet of REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register, within 2 business days. PRO-SBS-05 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) sets every step.
form.privacy:
We collect this information to support the provider that used a restrictive practice, and to review what happened with the participant. We also use it to decide whether the participant's behaviour support plan must change. Some of it is health information, which is sensitive.

The practitioner, the Clinical Supervisor, the Service Manager, the Quality Manager and the Chief Executive read this record. We tell the participant the outcome. We share it with family, other providers or other people only with consent, or where the law requires or allows it. We give information to the NDIS Commission when the law requires it.

If you are the participant, you can ask to see what we hold about you and ask us to correct it. You can say no to taking part. You can say no to other people being included. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect this record.
form.after:
• Service Manager: copy each answer marked for REG-SBS-01 to the incident review entry within 2 business days of receiving it (our standard).
  • Practitioner: complete Sections C and D within 12 business days of the notice (our standard).
  • Practitioner: complete Q30 and Q31 within 15 business days of the notice (our standard).
  • Clinical Supervisor: sign the findings and the outcome within 2 business days of Q31 (our standard).
  • Quality Manager: complete Q36 within 5 business days of the follow-up check, and close the record within 2 business days after that (our standard).
  • File the record on the participant's behaviour support file. Keep it for 7 years from the day it is closed (our standard).
  • That period matches the 7 years from the day a record is made in the Incident Rules, section 12(4), and the Restrictive Practices Rules, section 15(3).
  • Other law can require longer, for example for a record about a child. Check the law of [state or territory] before any record is destroyed.

register.proves:
This register is the one running record of every behaviour support plan [Provider name] writes. It has three sheets. On the plan sheet each row is one plan version. It shows when we were engaged and who wrote the plan. It shows what the participant agreed to and which accepted the plan. It shows whether the plan reached the Commissioner on time and when it is next due for . On the practice sheet each row is one in one plan, keyed on the plan number in col A, and holds the answers FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record routes here, with every status the practice has held. On the incident review sheet each row is one review under FRM-SBS-06 Restrictive Practice Incident Review Record of an emergency or , keyed on the plan number in col A.

"Behaviour Support Rules" here means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 40 (1) to s 40 (6). The register also holds the plan dates and records that s 39, s 41, s 42, s 43 and s 44 rely on. Those threads write to the columns marked with their indicators.
  • Legal basis: the Behaviour Support Rules. Sections 17 and 18 say who writes. Section 19 sets time limits. Section 20 says how plans are developed and section 21 what they contain. Sections 22 to 24 cover review, form and lodgement.
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years from the day the plan is superseded or ends (our standard). We set it to match the 7 years in section 15(3) of the Behaviour Support Rules for records of the use of a regulated restrictive practice.
  • Other law can require longer, for example for records about a child. For a participant under 18, keep the row until they turn 25 or for 7 years, whichever is later (our standard pending state law). Check REG-INF-02 Records Retention and Disposal Register and the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed.

Columns H and I are worked out and never typed over. Columns AB, AC, AD and AW are filled only when col Z lists a regulated restrictive practice, and summarise the practice sheet. 1. The Service Manager opens the row and keeps it. A sole does both. Open the row on the day we confirm the referral (our standard).
  2. Use one row for each plan version. A new version is a new row. Link it to the one it replaces in col D and col BD.
  3. The Practitioner gives each answer to the Service Manager within 1 of recording it on the form. The forms are FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template and FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record for the plan sheet, and FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record for the practice sheet. The Service Manager enters it within 2 business days of the stage (our standard).
  4. Columns that hold a list (col R, col Z, col AC, col AD, col AG, col AK, col AW and col BB, and practice sheet cols RP-P and RP-R) take a new dated line for each change. Never overwrite a line. An authorisation status is never typed over: every status the practice has held stays visible with its date.
  5. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  6. Never type over a worked-out date. To change the engagement date in col F, record the reason and the name of the who agreed.
  7. When systems are down, use the paper forms. The Service Manager enters them within 2 business days of the system coming back.
  8. When a row is about the work of the Service Manager or the Practitioner who keeps it, the Chief Executive holds it. When it is about the Chief Executive, the holds it. In a sole practitioner provider the Practitioner keeps every row, and the outside Clinical Supervisor reviews them every month under How we review.
  9. The practice sheet is the second sheet of this register: one row per regulated restrictive practice per plan, keyed on the plan number in col A, with cols RP-A to RP-R. Open a practice row when col Z first lists or proposes the practice. The incident review sheet is the third sheet: one row per FRM-SBS-06 review, keyed on col A, with cols IR-A to IR-O; open a row when a review starts and summarise it in col AZ. A small provider can keep the other list columns on a further sheet in the same way; each line carries the plan number from col A.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • the plan has been replaced by a later version that is in force, or the plan has ended, or the participant has left us, and col BD says which
  • every lodgement is done and recorded in col AO
  • every open line in col BB is done, or has moved to REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register with an owner and a due date
  • the Service Manager has checked the row and recorded the closing date.

register.rows: The rows are the data. They are kept in the workbook or system built to this specification, not in this document. The register has three sheets: the plan sheet (one row per plan version, cols A to BF), the practice sheet (one row per regulated restrictive practice per plan, cols RP-A to RP-R, keyed on col A) and the incident review sheet (one row per FRM-SBS-06 review, cols IR-A to IR-O, keyed on col A). Where a plan sheet cell would otherwise hold a list of practices or reviews, the second or third sheet holds the detail and the plan sheet cell summarises it. Every column name on the plan sheet is kept stable, because other documents cite the columns by name.
